title: ⚖️ AI mistakes a bag of chips for a gun... and four students sue the school and the police!
body: ⚖️ AI mistakes a bag of chips for a gun... and four students sue the school and the police!

Four students filed a lawsuit after an AI weapons-detection system mistook a bag of chips one of them was holding for a gun, and police surrounded them with weapons drawn, forced them to kneel, handcuffed them, and searched them, even though they had done nothing wrong.

The incident happened on the evening of October 20, 2025, outside Kenwood High School in Baltimore County, when the four students were waiting for a ride after football practice, sharing a bag of chips their coach had given one of them. The OmniAlert weapons-detection system raised an alert that there was a 90% chance of a gun at the school, even though school officials knew the system regularly issued false alerts. The school and police reviewed the image, decided the alert was wrong, and cancelled it — but armed police were still sent to the scene, because procedures did not stop an already-cancelled alert from being acted on. The lawsuit was filed on November 17, 2026, against the company, the school, the education department, the police, and officials, accusing them of violating the students' constitutional rights, unlawful arrest and search, and negligence, and demanding compensation, a ban on using the system until staff are trained, and a requirement that schools and police verify AI alerts before acting. The company declined to comment on the lawsuit.

Simply put: imagine the fire alarm in your house screaming every time you light the stove, so firefighters come and break down the door; that is how a false alert from an AI system turned into an armed confrontation with innocent students.
Do you support using AI weapons-detection systems in schools, or is the risk of error greater than the benefit?
